purpose.reader_question: When can remaining uncertainty leave the preferred action unchanged?
purpose.expected_reading: The crossing at theta=0.5 separates conditions preferring A and B. An interval spanning the crossing lacks a uniformly preferred action; either displayed one-sided interval has one.
purpose.claim: Under the two stipulated affine losses, ranking is stable over the one-sided compatible sets. This can support stopping inquiry about this uncertainty under the assumed model and other requirements.
purpose.scope: An illustrative two-action, single-condition calculation with both actions assumed feasible and lower loss preferred.
permitted_inferences: Threshold and ranking for the specified functions and intervals.
Conditional sufficiency for resolving this uncertainty about a uniform loss ranking.
prohibited_inferences: Empirical effectiveness of argumentation or of evidence acquisition.
A global minimum evidence set, evidence cost optimum, or a universal stopping rule.
Intervals are confidence intervals or a chronological acquisition sequence.
Absence of uniform preference prevents decisions under minimax or another decision rule.
Loss preference proves admissibility or supplies authority to act.

inputs.source_reference: Authored example supporting the accompanying engineering argumentation essay; values are stipulated, not measured.

quantities.label: theta
quantities.definition: Stipulated condition in [0,1]; compatible sets limit which values remain under consideration.

uncertainty.definition: Stipulated deterministic example, no statistical estimate.

quantities.label: L(A,theta)
quantities.definition: Stipulated loss for feasible action A.

uncertainty.definition: Stipulated deterministic example, no statistical estimate.

quantities.label: L(B,theta)
quantities.definition: Stipulated loss for feasible action B.

uncertainty.definition: Stipulated deterministic example, no statistical estimate.

constructions.definition: L(A,theta)=L(B,theta) iff theta=0.5 on [0,1]; both losses are 5 at the crossing. A has strictly lower loss for theta<0.5, B for theta>0.5; at equality the actions tie.
constructions.method: Solve 2+6*theta=5 exactly, then compare the affine difference 6*theta-3.

constructions.definition: Three distinct closed sets [0.2,0.8], [0.2,0.4] and [0.6,0.8]. Horizontal position and length encode endpoints and range. Vertical row is categorical, with no time or evidence-cost meaning.
constructions.method: Stipulate intervals and compare the affine loss difference at both endpoints; signs determine whether strict preference is uniform.

encodings.marks: Solid accent line for A and dashed dark line for B, each directly labelled.
encodings.represents: Each action loss as a function of theta in panel a.

scale_or_mapping.definition: Panel a uses x=theta linearly on [0,1] and y=L(action,theta) linearly on [0,8.5] arbitrary loss units.

encodings.marks: Fine grey dashed vertical line in both panels.

scale_or_mapping.definition: x=theta on a shared [0,1] domain; y length has no quantitative meaning for the threshold.

encodings.marks: Dark horizontal lines with perpendicular endpoint caps.

scale_or_mapping.definition: The endpoints are x=theta on [0,1]; interval length equals upper minus lower endpoint.

encodings.marks: Three vertically separated, directly labelled interval rows.

scale_or_mapping.definition: Top: preference varies; middle: A throughout; bottom: B throughout. No chronology, evidence strength or cost is encoded.
